incident-bot: :warning: P0 - KV cache correctness regression detected in prod (eu-central-1). Elevated client errors and malformed outputs. Trigger: anomaly detector on model-outcome-integrity.

incident-bot: Auto-alert at 1950123456 — creating incident thread.

maya (oncall): I'm on it. Paging @ryan @alex. What symptoms are we seeing?

ryan (eng-runtime): we've got reports of responses with tokens from previous requests interleaved. Also p50 latency fine but p99 shot up and some processes show >70% heap growth tied to kvcache.items. This started after the 07:10 deploy (commit def456).

alex (sre): I've correlated the spike with continuous-batcher throughput increase. Several batcher pods show abnormal cache hit rates for mismatched seq ranges. Looks like the cache key normalization dropped the session_id or seq_range in some paths. Potential cross-request KV reuse.

nina (support): Customers reporting errors: NovaRetail (~8% error increase) and HoloMed (~5%) with garbled completions. They've opened high-priority tickets asking if their inputs were mixed. We need to confirm/no data leakage ASAP.

ryan (eng-runtime): priority: confirm no data leakage and stop the faulty reuse quickly. Quick mitigation options: 
- toggle feature flag runtime.kv.disable_reuse=true (instant via config service)
- set continuous_batcher.enabled=false for critical shards (reduces batching but safe)
- orchestrated restart of batcher pool with a flush script
- emergency rollback of commit def456 (riskier timewise)

maya (oncall): What's fastest with minimal customer disruption?

alex (sre): Feature flag flip is fastest. It should stop reuse without restarting all pods. However, if stale entries remain in memory, we need a flush. I recommend: 1) set disable_reuse=true; 2) run targeted cache flush on the most impacted pool; 3) throttle continuous-batcher to reduce new pressure.

ryan (eng-runtime): prepared the config patch. Applying canary to two pods in eu-central-1 now. Command: 
```
configctl set runtime.kv.disable_reuse true --env prod --region eu-central-1 --canary 2
```
deploy-bot: configctl change applied by maya. Change id: cfg-7788. Canary started.

alex (sre): flushing caches on canary nodes: 
```
for pod in $(k get pods -n prod -l app=batcher -o name --region eu-central-1 | head -n 2); do \
  kubectl exec -n prod $pod -- /opt/redwood/bin/kv_flush --force &
  sleep 3
done
```

ryan (eng-runtime): canary telemetry: malformed-output-rate down on those pods ~6x. Heap growth stabilized. Good sign. Rolling to full pool with a 30s stagger.

nina (support): I sent an interim message to NovaRetail and HoloMed: "We observed inference integrity errors tied to a runtime cache reuse bug. We're deploying a hotfix now, mitigating impact. No evidence of cross-customer data persistence; we'll confirm after full rollout."

incident-bot: Status -> INVESTIGATING (1950123482)

maya (oncall): Rolling out config to remaining batchers. Watching metrics: request-error-rate and model-output-integrity.

ryan (eng-runtime): during rollout we started seeing a backlog on some shards because disable_reuse increases duplicate work. To avoid overload, temporarily reduced continuous_batcher.max_batch_size from 64 -> 24 and increased worker pool by +2 on hot nodes.

alex (sre): cluster pressure under control. p99 latency trending back to baseline in 8m. No further customer-visible errors reported after full rollout completed.

deploy-bot: config rollout cfg-7788 completed: success (1950123560). Details: https://deploys.internal/cfg/cfg-7788

nina (support): updating customers: "Hotfix applied; metrics normalized. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

ryan (eng-runtime): root cause initial analysis: commit def456 introduced a change that deduplicated KV keys but accidentally normalized away seq_range metadata when requests came through the path used by continuous-batcher head-of-line coalescing. That allowed cache entries to match incompatible requests (different seq offsets), causing returned KV blobs to be misaligned with current request state.

maya (oncall): any chance of secret/data mix between customers?

ryan (eng-runtime): we've audited memory snapshots and logs for identifiers; all reused entries were from same model-shard but different requests from same tenant pool — we haven't seen tenant A content served to tenant B. Still, mixed offsets cause corrupted outputs, which is serious. We'll add additional guards to the cache key to include seq_range and session nonce.

alex (sre): next steps (short-term): 
- keep runtime.kv.disable_reuse=true for 12-24h while we patch code
- add alert for kv_cache.unexpected_hit_with_seq_mismatch > 1/min
- add automated cache flush action on config flips

ryan (eng-runtime): medium-term: revert unsafe dedupe in def456 and replace with deterministic key composition including (tenant_id, model_version, seq_range_start, session_nonce). Add unit tests and an e2e continuous-batcher sim that asserts no cross-offset hits.

nina (support): I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and draft external postmortem for impacted accounts.

maya (oncall): Handoff: handing ops to ryan for monitoring window. I'll be offline for meeting in 1h. Alarms to watch: kv_cache.items, kv_cache.unexpected_hit_with_seq_mismatch, batcher.queue_length.

incident-bot: Status -> MITIGATED by ryan at 1950124020

ryan (eng-runtime): owners for postmortem: ryan (eng-runtime), alex (sre), nina (support). Draft ETA 72h. Action items created: ticket INF-8921 (fix key composition), INF-8922 (add tests), INF-8923 (add alert + auto-flush).

nina (support): customers notified at 1950123890 with summary and next steps.

maya (oncall): great triage. Closing thread unless new signals appear. :white_check_mark:
